texts: Waiting for a perimembranous VSD to close can lead to endocarditis, aortic insufficiency, pulmonary hypertension and failure to thrive: all of the above.
The jet through the defect injures the endocardium and invites endocarditis, and an aortic leaflet can prolapse into the hole and leak.
A large shunt floods the lungs, which can lead to pulmonary vascular disease, and the infant cannot feed and grow.
So small restrictive defects may be watched, but large ones, or any with leaflet prolapse or regurgitation, are closed.
In the picture, all four happen while the baby waits: the broccoli cards, the sagging mouth, the rising gauge and the thin baby.
Memory hook: waiting at the station, all four trains arrive.
